solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: In which rook may fly to mate? (5,5)

annotation.definition: In which rook may fly to mate?

blocks.note: the surface pictures a black bird in flight; the setter means the castle piece moved swiftly across the board
the surface suggests a bird seeking a partner; the setter means delivering checkmate

annotation.surface: A rook, the bird, flies off to find a partner.
annotation.walkthrough: Rook and mate read as birdlife and courtship; both are chess terms, and 'fly' describes how quickly the pieces move in a game against the clock.
annotation.definitionFit: Speed chess is chess played with very short time limits, so pieces fly towards mate.

entries.clue: Boarding houses confine children to keep quiet essentially (8)

indicatorNotes.to keep: to keep something is to hold it, so SONS holds the I within it
indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence, the middle, of quiet

annotation.surface: Boarding schools lock children up to keep them quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a verb after 'Boarding'; it is part of the plural definition. A pension is a continental boarding house.
annotation.definitionFit: Pensions are small European guesthouses or boarding houses.

entries.clue: Stopping for a smaller number of sheep (3)

indicatorNotes.Stopping for: the stopping, the filling, of the word

blocks.note: the middle of FEWER, a smaller number

annotation.surface: A farmer halts to count fewer sheep.
annotation.walkthrough: Stopping is filling, as in a tooth: the inside of fEWEr. 'A smaller number of' gives FEWER, which must be thought of before the middle is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a ewe is the female of the species, so any ewe is a sheep.

entries.clue: First hint of chest pain [in] store (5)

indicatorNotes.First hint of: take the first letter of chest

annotation.surface: A patient feels the first twinges of chest pain while in a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Store' sounds like a shop; here it is a hidden stockpile.
annotation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or weapons.

entries.clue: Turned out active men, working round ship in a group (2,5)

indicatorNotes.Turned out: only the outside of 'active' is used, its inside is thrown out
indicatorNotes.working: the letters are set to work in a new order

annotation.surface: Active soldiers turned out for work around a ship all together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' reads as 'showed up'; it strips 'active' to its outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A French phrase borrowed into English, literally 'in a mass', meaning everyone together at once.

entries.clue: Herb succeeded by saving a great deal of money (9)

indicatorNotes.saving: to save something is to keep it safe, so PER keeps the A tucked inside

blocks.note: per = by, as in per post
a mint is a vast sum

annotation.surface: A herb garden is taken over by a saver with a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded by' reads as one phrase; it splits into S and PER.
annotation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common garden mint used as a herb.

entries.clue: One half of crime mystery (4)

indicatorNotes.half of: keep only the second half of the word

blocks.note: the back half of WHODUNIT, a crime mystery

annotation.surface: A detective reckons only half the crime is a mystery.
annotation.walkthrough: A whodunit is a detective story; its eight letters split into WHOD and UNIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the counting sense: a unit is the number one, as in units, tens and hundreds.

entries.clue: Undesirable decision amended under FO checks (8-3)

indicatorNotes.amended: the letters are corrected into a new order
indicatorNotes.checks: the anagram holds CALL back inside itself

blocks.note: a referee's call is a decision

annotation.surface: An unwelcome ruling is revised after scrutiny by the Foreign Office.
annotation.walkthrough: The FO is the Foreign Office, the UK ministry for foreign affairs; here it is just two letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Uncalled-for means unwarranted and unwelcome, so undesirable.

entries.clue: Wretched person belonging to religious faction (6)

blocks.note: in a club = belonging to it
a sect is a religious faction

annotation.surface: A miserable soul joins a religious splinter group.
annotation.walkthrough: An insect is a contemptible person, a sense that is easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: Insect can be used for a worthless or despicable person.

entries.clue: Communication device beginning to malfunction on clapped-out Citroën (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, the M comes after the other part
indicatorNotes.clapped-out: a clapped-out car is worn out and falling apart, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: The radio in an old banger of a French car starts to go wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The diaeresis on Citroën is ignored. 'Clapped-out' is British slang for a worn-out old car.
annotation.definitionFit: An intercom is a device for speaking between rooms or parts of a building.

entries.clue: Exchange for notes and coins remains after banks in Elgin close as early as possible? (6)

indicatorNotes.banks in: the banks of Elgin are its edges, E and N
indicatorNotes.after: ASH is placed after the other letters

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning

annotation.surface: Someone wants cash before the banks in the Scottish town of Elgin shut for the day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banks' pretends to mean branches of banks in Elgin, a small town in Moray, Scotland; it is the letters at either side of the name.
annotation.definitionFit: To encash a cheque or bond is to exchange it for cash.

entries.clue: Thick rod in which nothing leaves dent (6)

indicatorNotes.in which: points to the rod as the word the O is taken from
indicatorNotes.leaves: the O goes away from POLE

annotation.surface: A thick rod that nothing can dent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like a description of the rod; it is a separate word meaning stupid, DIM.
annotation.definitionFit: A dimple is a small dent or hollow in a surface.

entries.clue: Ridiculing band turning up repeatedly during middle of night (4-7)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue the word runs upwards

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the night'

annotation.surface: A band keeps turning up in the middle of the night and is mocked for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a container instruction; it just gives IN.
annotation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it with scorn, ridiculing it.

entries.clue: Repeatedly cut extra diamonds [for] vestment (8)

indicatorNotes.Repeatedly cut: the last letter is cut off twice

blocks.note: SURPLUS, extra, loses its last two letters

annotation.surface: A jeweller keeps cutting extra diamonds to adorn a church robe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly cut' is two single-letter cuts, not one; SURPLUS becomes SURPL.
annotation.definitionFit: A surplice is a loose white linen vestment worn over a cassock by clergy and choristers.

entries.clue: Somehow he felt done in where going on would be futile (3,2,3,4)

annotation.definition: where going on would be futile

indicatorNotes.Somehow: the letters come together some other way

annotation.surface: Someone feels exhausted and sees no point carrying on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Done in' means exhausted, which fits the definition so well that the anagram is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: The end of the line is the point beyond which nothing more can be done.

entries.clue: Betrayer[’s] characteristic concerning heads of Security Service (9)

indicatorNotes.heads of: the first letters of Security and Service

annotation.surface: The mark of a traitor is her dealings with the Security Service.
annotation.walkthrough: The Security Service is MI5, the UK's domestic intelligence agency, which fits the traitor picture; here it gives only its initials.
annotation.definitionFit: The -ess ending marks a woman; a traitress is a woman who betrays, and the clue's gender-neutral word covers her.

entries.clue: Look of disapproval about withdrawn support capital (8)

indicatorNotes.about: FROWN goes round the other part
indicatorNotes.withdrawn: TEE is drawn back, reading upwards

blocks.note: a frown is a look of disapproval
TEE, a golf ball's support, reversed

annotation.surface: A frown greets the news that financial support for the capital has been pulled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Support' is the golfer's tee, not money.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the West African port founded for freed slaves is the seat of government of Sierra Leone.

entries.clue: Stage production of Dante’s Inferno maybe put oneself at risk (4,4,4)

annotation.definition: Stage production of Dante’s Inferno maybe

blocks.clueFragment: Stage production of Dante’s Inferno maybe
blocks.note: a drama whose setting is Hell, a place full of flames

annotation.surface: A theatre company staging Dante's vision of Hell is taking a gamble.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: the Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, set in a burning Hell.
annotation.definitionFit: To play with fire is to take foolish risks.

entries.clue: Dodgy dealer[’s] extra float picked up (4,3)

indicatorNotes.picked up: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: a wide is an extra in cricket, a run for a ball bowled out of reach

annotation.surface: A shady dealer offers an extra float for the till.
annotation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a small-time crook or spiv. BUOY is said 'boy' in British English.
annotation.definitionFit: A wide boy is a man who lives by petty crime and shady deals.

entries.clue: Help mainly supported by one Umbrian town (6)

indicatorNotes.mainly: most of the word, the last letter dropped
indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue the I sits beneath

blocks.note: ASSIST, help, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A small Italian town relies on one benefactor for most of its aid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supported by' is a down-clue placement: the I goes under ASSIS.
annotation.definitionFit: Assisi, home of St Francis, is a hill town in Umbria, Italy.

entries.clue: Classified ad covering second excursion that avoids island (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: AD goes over, outside, the other letters
indicatorNotes.that avoids: the I is left out of SORTIE

blocks.note: SORTIE, an excursion, without I for island

annotation.surface: A classified advert for a trip that skips the island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Classified ad' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Classified' alone, meaning sorted.
annotation.definitionFit: Assorted can mean sorted into classes, classified.

entries.clue: Moved to act after sons welled up (6)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following in order, so URGED is written following the S

annotation.surface: Parents are stirred to act after their sons become tearful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moved to act' is one unit, URGED; 'to' is not a link word here.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe water, or an emotion, rising and pouring forward.

entries.clue: Eastern European getting tummy upset over outburst (5)

indicatorNotes.getting tummy upset: the tummy, the middle of SLAV, is turned over
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue O comes under the rest

blocks.note: SLAV with its middle letters L and A swapped

annotation.surface: An Eastern European with an upset stomach has an outburst.
annotation.walkthrough: The tummy is the middle of the word, so only LA is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A salvo is a sudden burst, of gunfire or of words.

entries.clue: Old instrument with ridges mostly seen outside India (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: 'mostly' means not quite all, so the word is used minus its final letter
indicatorNotes.seen outside: to be seen outside something is to be around it, so RIBBE wraps the I

blocks.note: RIBBED, with ridges, less its last letter
I is India in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An old ribbed instrument turns up on the outskirts of India.
annotation.walkthrough: A ribibe is obscure, so trust the wordplay: RIB(I)BE.
annotation.definitionFit: The ribibe was a medieval bowed string instrument, related to the rebec.

entries.clue: Cycling laden, runs into marsh creature (8)

indicatorNotes.Cycling: the first letter of FULL is moved round to the end

blocks.note: FULL, laden, with F moved to the end

annotation.surface: A laden cyclist rides into a swamp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marsh creature' reads as one phrase, but 'marsh' is wordplay, BOG, and the definition is just 'creature'. FULL cycles by moving its first letter to the back.
annotation.definitionFit: The bullfrog is a large frog of ponds and marshes.

entries.clue: Note female that amazes me (3)

blocks.note: ah is what you say in wonder

annotation.surface: A woman's singing voice amazes the listener.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That amazes me' is a whole phrase standing for an exclamation.
annotation.definitionFit: Fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale.

entries.clue: Part of spectrum in glaze of certain pottery (4)

indicatorNotes.Part of: the answer is a piece of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A potter admires a band of colour in the glaze of a vase.
annotation.walkthrough: The glaze sounds like the pottery's own, but only its G is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Ming porcelain, made under China's Ming dynasty, is a prized kind of pottery.

entries.clue: Work unexpectedly on the sly secures one way to get a buzz? (10)

indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: the letters fall into an unexpected order
indicatorNotes.secures: the anagram holds OP inside it

annotation.surface: Someone secretly takes a job for the thrill of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' suggests a thrill; it is the reedy electronic sound of a stylophone, a small toy keyboard played with a stylus.
annotation.definitionFit: The Stylophone is a pocket synthesiser whose buzzing tone is its trademark, hence the question mark.
